title: Lexer table
description: How the table-driven lexer splits the source of one language into tokens: comments, string and character literals, string templates, identifiers, keywords and operators. Whitespace is skipped; anything not described is a single-character punctuation token. The pack manifest says which table applies to which file name extensions.

language.description: Language identifier, as in the languages of the pack manifest.

lineComment.description: Opener of a comment that runs to the end of the line. Absent: the language has none.

blockComment.description: Comment between an opener and a closer, possibly over several lines. An unterminated one ends at the end of the file. Absent: the language has none.

nested.description: True if an opener inside the comment opens a nested comment that needs its own closer.

docComment.description: Opener of a block comment that is a documentation comment, for example /**. It must start with the block comment opener; a comment that closes right after the opener (/**/) is a plain block comment.

strings.description: String literal forms. The longest matching delimiter wins.

items.description: One string literal form, opened and closed by the same delimiter.

delimiter.description: Opening and closing delimiter, for example " or """.

escape.description: Escape character: it and the character after it are content. Absent: the form has no escapes.

raw.description: True if the literal is a raw string or text block token rather than a plain string token.

multiline.description: True if the literal may span lines; it then ends at the end of the file when unterminated. False: an unterminated literal ends at the end of its line.

templates.description: True if the literal may contain template expressions, as described by templates.

greedyClose.description: True if delimiter characters right after a closing delimiter still belong to the literal, which then ends at the last of them (Kotlin: """a"""" is the raw string a").

char.description: Character literal. An unterminated one ends at the end of its line. Absent: the language has none.

delimiter.description: Opening and closing delimiter, for example '.

escape.description: Escape character: it and the character after it are content.

quotedIdentifier.description: Delimiter of an identifier that may contain any character but a line break, for example the backtick in Kotlin. Absent: the language has none.

templates.description: Template expressions inside the string forms that allow them. Required if any string form has templates.

identifier.description: Prefix of a template made of one identifier, for example $ in $name.

open.description: Opener of a template expression, for example ${. The expression is lexed as code.

close.description: Closer of a template expression, for example }. Braces opened inside the expression must close first.

identifierChars.description: Characters, besides letters, digits and the underscore, that may appear in an identifier, for example $ in Java.

softKeywords.description: Words that are keywords only in some places; they are identifier tokens flagged as soft keywords.

operators.description: Operators and punctuation of more than one character, matched longest first. Other punctuation is one token per character.

lexerMarker.description: A fixed sequence of non-blank characters that opens or closes a token.

lexerWords.description: Distinct words made of letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.
